# Authored model fixtures

`triangle.stl` is an authored CC0 triangle with vertices (-1,-1,0), (1,-1,0), (0,1,0), source normal (0,0,1), and bounds [-1,-1,0] to [1,1,0]. It has no physical units or color extension. It is suitable for a visible window/orbit smoke check, not representative of large-model loading speed.

Seven CC0 OBJ files and their `triangles.f32le` surface oracles are generated by `scripts/generate-obj-fixtures.py`. The manifest identifies five independent trimesh 4.11.2 readbacks and two authored concave-surface references. Oracle triangulation may use a different diagonal or internal vertices; signed area, bounds, coverage and U-shape GPU pixels are the equivalence contracts. Source UV/normal/material-state retention has separate authored expectations. Reproduction requires the external fixture Python environment with numpy and pinned trimesh; it adds no runtime dependency.

Twelve PLY files, native-property byte/schema readbacks and float64 triangle references are generated by `scripts/generate-ply-fixtures.py`, using pinned plyfile 1.1.3 as an independent reader. Binary bytes are authored explicitly to avoid its scalar-writer endian issue with the installed numpy. Authored coordinates are also asserted during generation. The sources cover ASCII/LE/BE, all eight numeric types, unknown list/edge properties, ancillary NaN payloads, reordered fields, float64 translation and concave contours. Raw column bytes and declared schema are exact contracts; concave tessellation uses an authored rectangle reference. These fixtures are CC0 and do not add runtime dependencies.

Seven CC0 OFF sources and float64 triangle references are generated by `scripts/generate-off-fixtures.py`. Four use pinned trimesh 4.11.2 geometry readback; the binary/attribute and U-contour references have explicit authored expectations. The decoder checks winding and surface coverage independently of triangulation diagonal, and exact authored normals/colors/UV/index data. The manifest carries source/oracle SHA-256 values. The fixture environment adds no runtime dependency.
